chunks: And as for what Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah about shortening (al-taqseer) and completing (al-timmam) the prayer in the two Holy Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina). He said: 'Do not complete (the prayer) until you intend to stay for ten days.' I said: 'Indeed, our companions narrated from you that you ordered them to complete (the prayer).' He said: 'Indeed, your companions would enter the mosque, pray, take their sandals, and leave, while the people were facing them (entering the mosque for prayer). So I ordered them to complete (the prayer). The explanation of this report is that completing the prayer is not obligatory except for one who intends to stay for ten days. And whoever does not intend that is free to choose between completing and shortening, even though completing is superior. And his saying (peace be upon him) to one who would leave the mosque at the time of prayer and not pray with the people was an order of obligation, and it was not permissible for him to leave it, for one whose way is this, because in doing so there is repelling taqiyyah (divine precaution), encouraging the self, and disparaging the school (of thought). And that is what reveals what we mentioned, that this (ruling) came out as taqiyyah.'

key_terms.الْإِتْمَام: The act of completing the prayer
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Holy Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening or completing prayers in Mecca and Medina according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves the apparent contradiction in hadiths by distinguishing between the general permission to shorten prayers for travelers and the specific obligation to complete them for those who explicitly intend a ten-day stay. He further elucidates that the command to complete for those merely leaving the mosque was a case of *taqiyyah* (divine precaution), designed to prevent the appearance of negligence and to protect the reputation of the Shia school from criticism by the general populace.
